s.en: remove a user or group from the system

syn: deluser [--backup] [--backup-suffix str] [--backup-to dir] [--conf file] [--debug] [--remove-all-files] [--remove-home] [--quiet] [--verbose] [--stdoutmsglevel prio] [--stderrmsglevel prio] [--logmsglevel prio] [--lock] user ⏎ deluser [--system] [--backup] [--backup-suffix str] [--backup-to dir] [--conf file] [--debug] [--remove-all-files] [--remove-home] [--quiet] [--verbose] [--stdoutmsglevel prio] [--stderrmsglevel prio] [--logmsglevel prio] [--lock] [--force-delete] user ⏎ deluser --group [--conf file] [--debug] [--only-if-empty] [--quiet] [--verbose] [--stdoutmsglevel prio] [--stderrmsglevel prio] [--logmsglevel prio] group ⏎ delgroup [--system] [--conf file] [--debug] [--only-if-empty] [--quiet] [--verbose] [--stdoutmsglevel prio] [--stderrmsglevel prio] [--logmsglevel prio] group ⏎ deluser [--conf file] [--debug] [--quiet] [--verbose] [--stdoutmsglevel prio] [--stderrmsglevel prio] [--logmsglevel prio] user group ⏎ deluser --help

o.en: Backup all files contained in the userhome and the mailspool file to a file named username.tar.bz2 or username.tar.gz. Valid modes: deluser, deluser --system.
Select compression algorithm for a home directory backup. Can be set to any suffix recognized by tar --auto-compress. Defaults to .gz. Valid modes: deluser, deluser --system.
Place the backup files not in the current directory but in dir. This implicitly sets --backup also. Defaults to the current working directory. Valid modes: deluser, deluser --system.
Use file instead of the default files /etc/deluser.conf and /etc/adduser.conf. Multiple --conf options may be given.
Remove a group. This is the default action if the program is invoked as delgroup. Valid mode: deluser.
Only remove if no members are left. Valid modes: deluser --group, delgroup.

Remove all files from the system owned by this user. Note: --remove-home does not have an effect any more. If --backup is specified, the files are deleted after having performed the backup. Valid modes: deluser, deluser --system.
Remove the home directory of the user and its mailspool. If --backup is specified, the files are deleted after having performed the backup. Valid modes: deluser, deluser --system.
Only delete if user/group is a system user/group. If the user does not exist, no error value is returned. Valid modes: deluser, deluser --system.

Minimum priority for messages logged to syslog/journal and the console, respectively. Values are trace, debug, info, warn, err, and fatal. Messages with the priority set here or higher get printed to the respective medium. Messages printed to stderr are not repeated on stdout.

If deluser is called with the --lock option, the user account will be locked rather than removed. In this case, the user's password is invalidated and the account is set to expired; no other action is taken. A locked account may be subsequently unlocked using adduser --unlock.
